prompt: Create ONE production-ready illustrated game sprite atlas image for a warm medieval magical bird-led realm, Kingdom of Alderwing. EXACT regular 4-column by 4-row grid, square image; 16 evenly sized square cells, each object fully inside its cell with generous empty margin, centered. TRUE TRANSPARENT RGBA background outside each object, absolutely NO checkerboard baked in, no backdrop, no grid lines, no labels, no letters, no text. Consistent detailed hand-painted 2D adventure-game cutout art, opaque richly colored surfaces, crisp dark ink silhouette, brass highlights, warm aged timber, teal cloth, parchment cream, jewellike accents. Front-facing slightly three-quarter view but grounded objects, readable from far away. These are actual small world objects, not flat emojis or abstract interface glyphs. Row1 left-to-right: carved timber request noticeboard with rolled parchment and gold wax feather seal; closed brass-trimmed oak treasure chest; curled parchment lore scroll tied with teal ribbon; small leather satchel with brass buckle and peeking paper. Row2: antique brass bell on small timber bracket; warm amber glass lantern; hanging wooden wind chime with three brass reeds; standing rune stone with inset teal leaf carving. Row3: ornate small secret puzzle casket with three colored circular buttons; terracotta planter of green ivy and a small bloom; wooden spool with trailing red festival ribbon; weathered brass gear and wooden repair mallet together. Row4: forked wooden trail signpost with teal wayfinding arrows; folded parchment map with red path line and compass rose (NO text); round carved medallion with feather relief; ceramic blue bowl beside smooth colored river pebbles. Uniform camera angle, all fully visible, no shadow casting outside silhouette, no cropped pieces, no intercell overlap. Treat as a single coherent professionally painted 16-cell atlas asset for alpha-tested world sprites.
encoding: Lossless WebP encoding only; original dimensions and all alpha values retained. Explicit UV rectangles in village_discoveries.js follow the original irregular atlas packing.
